notes.note: Tests the basic form 'var template <Type> <id> := ...'; the initialization is included because the syntactical structure requires it.
Ambiguity: the syntax block makes ':=' TemplateBody mandatory, so the test only shows that an initial content is assigned at declaration and used; it does not test omitting the initialization.

Titan warning is wrong: Titan rejects @deterministic on template variables and a template variable declaration without TypeOrNestedTypeDef ('var template v_e := 5;'), but both are allowed by the 11.2 syntactical structure.
Titan warning is wrong: Titan does not implement concatenation of charstring templates containing AnyValue (clause 15.11 allows it; "ab" & ? produces a pattern).
Ambiguity: literal reading chosen; the test assigns a template variable to a plain value variable.

Because the declaration syntax requires initialization, an uninitialized template variable is represented by a field left uninitialized with '-' (the template variable as a whole is partially initialized). Using that field in match() is the error. Treated as a runtime error (ttcn3verdict:error).

Titan warning: Titan does not check that a template variable used in receive is completely initialized. The violation (field left uninitialized with '-') can be determined statically, so this is a reject test; a tool might detect it only at runtime.
Uses restriction 15.0 a), following the 15.0 example: a template for a type that contains a default field. Titan does not implement this check.
Titan warning: Titan does not implement @fuzzy/@deterministic checks for template variables used in a snapshot (receive in alt).
Applied to a template variable of a structured address type initialized with null; the field reference on the right hand side causes a runtime error.

Titan warning: Titan does not detect initialization from an unbound variable at compile time. The violation is statically determinable, so this is a reject test; a tool might detect it only at runtime.
The general syntax already makes ':=' mandatory, so this test also violates the syntactical structure; the test cannot isolate restriction n).
Ambiguity: literal reading chosen (runs on the same component type; extended component types are not tested).
Ambiguity: the general reading covers start values too, but the test uses a negative default duration in the declaration because that is statically checkable. A negative start value is not covered.
The timer ceasing to exist is observed indirectly: after the function returns, 'any timer.running' is false.
Titan warning is wrong: Titan does not support operations through timer references (timer type, clause 6.2.14) such as vc_t.running.
A timer that no longer exists cannot be referenced, so 'stops running' is observed only through 'any timer.running' being false.
Ambiguity: elements skipped with '-' are excluded; the test uses a negative element value.
